extracted.intended_audience: research funders, peer reviewers, research administrators, and interdisciplinary researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative checklists for assessing deeply integrative interdisciplinary research (IDR), focused on grant proposals, research outputs, careers, centres, and national research assessment exercises. Provides question-sets, implementation recommendations, and higher-level classification of evaluative dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core question: emergent whole greater than sum of parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project, centre or output successfully and effectively integrate its disciplinary components, so that it generates an emergent whole, addressing an interdisciplinary research question, and producing outcomes that are demonstrably greater than the sum of its (disciplinary) parts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the summative core issue for IDR evaluation; evaluations should attend to integration, mutual dependency, co-generation of questions, and whether outputs cannot be expressed as merely disciplinary contributions in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q1: quality dimensions (goals, method, results, presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal describe clear goals, adequate preparation, appropriate method, significant results, effective presentation, reflective critique?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general checklist-style probe addressing standard research quality dimensions, applied with an IDR lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q2: problem formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the problem formulated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess co-generation of research questions and whether problem formulation integrates disciplinary perspectives rather than imposing a single-discipline framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q3: diversity and suitability of disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: How diverse are the disciplines, methods and researchers and how suitable is the combination of disciplines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether the chosen disciplinary mix is justified and appropriate to the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q4: justification for choice of disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a clear justification for the choice of disciplines based on the needs of the research questions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit rationale showing discipline selection driven by research needs, not convenience or tokenism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q5: anchoring in relevant literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the study sufficiently anchored in relevant literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check interdisciplinary grounding across relevant fields and literatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q6: relationship with methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the relationship with the methodology?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how disciplinary methods relate and are integrated; consider mixed-methods coherence and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q7: communication plan
rubrics_metrics.description: How will communication be tackled?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate plans for intra-team communication, translation across disciplinary languages, and mechanisms for mutual understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q8: description of integration of disciplinary insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it describe how the insights of the disciplines involved will be integrated (in the design and conduct of the research as well as in subsequent publications) and how this relates to the type of interdisciplinarity involved; does it demonstrate how the quality of integration will be assured?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit mechanisms for integration (analytical synthesis, joint interpretation, combined outputs) and quality-assurance for integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q9: collaboration organisation and awareness of integration challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: How is the collaboration organized — is there an understanding of the challenges of interdisciplinary integration, including methodological integration, and the 'human' side of fostering interactions and communication, and an effective strategy to achieve this?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess governance, roles, facilitation, training, and explicit strategies for the social dimensions of collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q10: leadership and management strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the leadership role and management strategy to deliver the desired outcomes clearly articulated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate leadership capacity, clarity of responsibilities, and management structures suited to IDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q11: interdisciplinary skills and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the researchers involved have demonstrable interdisciplinary skills and experience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check track records and evidence of prior interdisciplinary practice, training, or successful integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q12: evidence of interdisciplinary leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: In particular, is there evidence of interdisciplinary leadership?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for leaders who have led integrative projects and can mediate across disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q13: stakeholder/user engagement plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an appropriate plan for stakeholder/user engagement from the outset of the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess involvement of external partners, co-design, and relevance to non-academic stakeholders where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q14: budgeting for additional resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the proposal budget for, and justify, the additional resources needed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit justification for extra time, personnel, translation, facilitation, or infrastructure IDR entails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lyall & King Q15: interdisciplinarity reflected in outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clear how interdisciplinarity will be reflected in the project outputs and outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check intended forms of publication, integrated outputs, and dissemination strategies that reflect integration rather than separate disciplinary products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 1: emergent whole criterion (Is the emergent whole greater?)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the emergent whole of the IDR greater than or different from the sum of its parts? Do the ingredient disciplines do more than work in parallel but interact, communicate, recombine? Are they sufficient?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central Durham checklist item emphasizing integration; look for evidence of interaction, recombination, and genuine synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 2: inclusive leadership structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the leadership structure characterized by inclusivity, facilitation, transparency of roles and an equality of contributing disciplines in terms of voice and status?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether leadership avoids dominance by one discipline and fosters equal contribution and voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 3: resources/time for dialogue and co-learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Are additional resources and time planned for dialogue, co-learning and integration between the contributing disciplines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require clear provision for activities that enable integration (meetings, training, translation work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 4: disciplinary benefit on own terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clear how the individual disciplines may benefit on their own terms by engaging with the IDR, noting that this can be transformational?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reciprocal benefits to participating disciplines and whether engagement is transformative rather than extractive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 5: disciplinary hospitality
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a disciplinary hospitality between the researchers, and to external participants, which avoids a hierarchical view of the contributing disciplines?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for culture and practices that respect and welcome differing epistemologies and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 6: support for social cohesion of collaborators
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there ways of supporting the social cohesion of the collaborators (recognizing that interdisciplinary support structures may help)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess mechanisms for team-building, mentoring, conflict resolution, and community-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 7: recognition of different scales and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Have the different scales, and communication between them, been recognized in the structure of the research?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cross-scale communication (e.g., local vs. global, lab vs. community) and structures to manage them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 8: processes for cohering different data
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there processes for cohering the different data in the research, quantitative and qualitative, recognizing the need for translation where this is necessary?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit strategies for data integration, mixed-data synthesis, and translation across methodologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 9: representation of IDR experience and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the necessary experience with IDR represented by the team and the leadership as well as training and development in place?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess both current experience and plans for building capacity (training, development) in interdisciplinary skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 10: openness and flexibility in research plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Are research plans sufficiently open and flexible to adapt to new questions or directions that might arise unforeseen at the outset?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value adaptive designs and contingency planning appropriate to emergent IDR pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durham IAS 11: role of 'service disciplines' driven by project needs
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are 'service disciplines' identified in the research, has this been driven by the project needs and not by assumed prevalence of one discipline over another?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guard against marginalizing certain disciplines by ensuring any serving role is justified by research needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belcher et al. category: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how relevant the research is to the problems or contexts it aims to address (part of Belcher et al.'s framework for transdisciplinarity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate alignment with real-world problems, stakeholder needs, and the practical aims of the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belcher et al. category: Credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific/technical credibility of the research (part of Belcher et al.'s framework).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check methodological rigor, evidence, and plausibility across contributing disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belcher et al. category: Legitimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of procedural fairness, stakeholder inclusion, and trustworthiness (Belcher et al.'s category containing many IDR-specific requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine stakeholder engagement, transparency, and recognition of normative/ethical dimensions of research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Belcher et al. category: Effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of outcomes, including training and development and capacity-building aspects of IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the research achieves intended objectives and builds sustained capability for interdisciplinary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: King (2008) principle 1: variability of goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that interdisciplinary projects have variable goals which should be assessed in their own terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid one-size-fits-all indicators; tailor evaluation to project-specific objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: King (2008) principle 2: variability of criteria and indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept that criteria and indicators may legitimately vary across IDR projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use flexible, context-sensitive metrics rather than rigid discipline-centric indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: King (2008) principle 3: leveraging of integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the extent to which integration leverages new knowledge/value beyond disciplinary inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for evidence that integration leads to added-value outcomes not achievable by single disciplines alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: King (2008) principle 4: interaction of social and cognitive factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the social (communication, collaboration) and cognitive (epistemic, conceptual) interactions that enable integration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assessment of team dynamics, communication norms, and epistemic negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: King (2008) principle 5: management, leadership, and coaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess management structures, leadership, and coaching that facilitate interdisciplinary work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether there is active management and mentorship of integration processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: King (2008) principle 6: iteration in a comprehensive and transparent system
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate iterative processes and transparency in project development and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage cyclical refinement, open documentation, and transparent decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: King (2008) principle 7: effectiveness and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the effectiveness of the research and its impacts (academic and non-academic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both short- and long-term impacts, and whether evaluation captures non-linear pathways to impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate multiple disciplinary expertise concurrently
rubrics_metrics.description: The need to evaluate multiple disciplinary expertise in linked and concurrent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should be able to judge how disciplinary skills are combined in real time, not just assessed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate deployment of mixed methodologies
rubrics_metrics.description: The deployment of mixed methodologies arising from disparate disciplines must be assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine coherence, compatibility, and translation between quantitative and qualitative or other distinct methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate team-building and management (disciplinary hospitality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require evaluation of team-building and management arrangements, including 'disciplinary hospitality'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how team culture, inclusivity, and mentorship support integration and equality between disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate timeframe, size, and cost differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The more extended timeframe, size and cost typical of IDR projects, and the differing temporal needs of disciplinary areas, should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure budgets and timelines account for integration activities, and reviewers do not penalize longer or costlier IDR for legitimate reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate role of external participants
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to evaluate the role of participants external to the academic team (especially important in TDR and 'challenge-driven' IDR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess non-academic partner contributions, their legitimacy, and how they are integrated into research design and outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate equality and productive partnerships between disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the achievement of equality and productive partnerships between disciplines in contexts of differing status and access to resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit measures to prevent dominance, ensure fair resource allocation, and equitable recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate framing of outputs within single-discipline frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: The limited ability to frame the outputs and outcomes of IDR within the existing evaluation frameworks of the participating single disciplines must be recognised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reviewers to judge outputs on interdisciplinary merits rather than forcing disciplinary proxies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate language accessibility for evaluators
rubrics_metrics.description: Require that IDR projects frame outputs and proposals in language accessible to potential evaluators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for clear explanations, glossaries, and translation of discipline-specific jargon to enable fair review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect and avoid token disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert to the occasional involvement of 'token' disciplines in response to inadequately framed IDR funding calls or misconceived responses to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether each disciplinary contribution is substantive and necessary, not merely symbolic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage multiplicity of criteria in IDR proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the bewildering multiplicity of criteria that arise in IDR proposals and accommodate them in evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use structured question-sets or layered frameworks to handle multiple evaluative strands coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid double or multiple jeopardy in sequential single-discipline evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of the danger of double, or multiple, jeopardy in the sequential evaluation of IDR through single-disciplinary lenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assessment pipelines that filter IDR through separate disciplinary hurdles before integrative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider journal prestige and publication incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the perception that interdisciplinary journals may be lower profile and the disincentive this creates for publishing IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not penalize IDR for lower-impact-factor outlets if outputs demonstrate integration and quality; consider alternative impact measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require openness, flexibility, and contingencies
rubrics_metrics.description: The increased need for openness and flexibility in IDR and the consequent complexity of planning contingencies and risk-mitigation should be evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess project adaptability and realistic contingency planning for emergent research paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and manage incompatible criteria across evaluating bodies
rubrics_metrics.description: Be alert to the occasional simultaneous presence of more than one evaluating body with incompatible criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, harmonize criteria or provide cross-walks so IDR is not penalized by conflicting evaluation expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid parallelism without integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Beware the risk that disciplinary components of a project may simply proceed in parallel, without intensive interaction and mutual dependency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concrete integration activities and shared outputs rather than parallel, siloed workstreams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use question-based frameworks for IDR evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Frameworks for evaluating IDR commonly take the form of question-sets addressing holistic structures of good IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt structured question-sets (like those presented) to probe integration, leadership, resources, and outputs across levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appraise team science proposals holistically
rubrics_metrics.description: Team science grant proposals need to be appraised holistically, as well as from the perspective of the relevant disciplines (Academy of Medical Sciences recommendation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure panels assess both disciplinary rigour and integrative, emergent outcomes in a concerted manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train and induct peer and panel reviewers and grant managers
rubrics_metrics.description: Funders should induct and train peer and panel reviewers, as well as grant managers, to meet the challenge of evaluating IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training on interdisciplinary criteria, integration assessment, and how to interpret mixed-methods and cross-disciplinary outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select reviewers with translation and IDR experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ reviewers who have experience of 'translation' between the languages of different disciplines and of the nature of well-integrated and high-quality IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reviewers who have led effective IDR themselves or have documented integrative practice; include 'integrative' reviewers alongside disciplinary experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange referees to communicate to produce a single assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange for referees to communicate in the production of a single assessment of an IDR proposal, rather than producing individual assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate joint referee discussions or collaborative reporting to capture integrative judgements coherently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow proposers to respond to individual referee comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that proposers are able to address, in writing, comments by individual referees before a proposal is assessed or ranked by a panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rebuttal or response stages to clarify misunderstandings and provide evidence of integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include user-community or non-academic reviewers on panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Include user-community or other non-academic reviewers on panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring stakeholder perspectives and practical relevance into assessment, especially for challenge-driven IDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 2-stage review processes that place disciplinary hurdles first
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid '2-stage' review processes for IDR, in which a single-disciplinary hurdle is placed before the integrative evaluation of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent filtering that forces IDR to conform to disciplinary criteria before integration can be judged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate communication between referees and panels about IDR criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate between referees and panels to ensure that they individually and corporately understand the process and criteria of IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use briefings, shared rubrics, or moderators to align understanding of IDR-specific evaluation dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider track records of research leaders for IDR experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the track records of the researchers, especially of the research leaders, for experience in IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use leadership CVs and prior outputs to assess capacity to manage integrative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on quantitative publication measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid reliance on quantitative publication measures, such as citation rates and impact factors, when evaluating IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use qualitative assessment of integration and broader measures of impact and effectiveness appropriate to IDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probe institutional support and development structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Probe beyond the research proposals to consider the support and development structures, such as centres and institutes, of the institution(s) in which the research will be pursued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate institutional incentives, infrastructure, and policies that enable sustained IDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create interdisciplinary panels for national evaluations
rubrics_metrics.description: Create one or more explicitly interdisciplinary panels, either welcoming any IDR-flagged outputs, or focusing on integrative topics such as 'energy', 'security', 'global policy', 'biophysical sciences'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A national-scale remedy that concentrates expertise to judge emergent integrative outputs effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deploy pool of panel members with interdisciplinary expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and deploy a pool of panel members with strong interdisciplinary expertise and experience, either within a focused IDR panel and/or with members on all subject panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dedicated interdisciplinary experts to adjudicate integration across panels or to advise disciplinary panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine 'output' and 'impact' evaluation for non-academic partner IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of IDR with non-academic partners, create evaluatory structures that do not differentiate the categories of 'output' and 'impact' as strongly as at present, but combine them in ways that respond to the non-linear nature of IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess co-produced knowledge and practical impacts together, reflecting non-linear pathways from research to societal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include explicit examination of institutional incentives for IDR
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating the research environment of institutions, include an explicit and detailed examination of the incentives for building IDR, including support for interdisciplinary communities, centres, and career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reward institutional policies and structures that foster healthy IDR ecosystems and career pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build evaluative messages that support IDR into national criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Research evaluation exercises at national scale should build strong evaluative messages into their criteria that support highly effective IDR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use national criteria and communications to shape incentives favoring integration, not disciplinary-only rewards.
